assessments.reasoning: The actual Xerox PARC print heading and date identify MPL(B). Its introduction names MAXC and PDP-10 and describes a limited extension of MPL(A), explicitly cast as interim and intended to work with subsequent versions.

challenge.method: Check the part and page stamps visually, distinguish stated intent from successful compatibility, compare the direct September 1972 MPS 11.0 manual and inspect the relevant CHM bibliography and footnote.
challenge.results: The 1972 source is labeled MPS and includes distinct provenance. The 1974 MPL(B) page supplies the exact scoped language-line identity. The CHM narrative’s footnote citation points to the MPS debugger bibliography entry, while the bibliography links the inspected MPL(B) text separately. This reference discrepancy leaves the directly inspected page decisive.

limitations: The exact print supports a named language line, without establishing purpose or language identity of every item at the archive heading, compatibility, or a precise identity for MPS or MPL(A).
